title: Error Analysis of Globally Distributed Workflow Management System
problem: Globally distributed workflow management systems (like PanDA for ATLAS/LHC) face significant challenges from faults and errors occurring across heterogeneous sites. Error analysis is essential for designing effective mitigation strategies.
motivation: The ATLAS experiment at LHC produces massive data requiring distributed processing across the Worldwide LHC Computing Grid. Errors occur frequently in distributed systems but systematic analysis is lacking, hindering reliability improvements.
method: The researchers examined errors that actually occurred in the PanDA workflow management system, which coordinates computational work across computing sites distributed globally. They collected data on failures across all these different sites and organized them into categories based on type (network problems, resource shortages, software bugs, etc.). By analyzing which types of errors happened most frequently and where, they identified patterns in how large-scale distributed systems fail. This systematic error mapping is essential for designing defenses against future failures.
key_novelty: This analysis systematically characterizes the types of errors and failure patterns that occur in production-scale distributed workflow systems across heterogeneous computing sites.
contributions: Systematic error analysis in globally distributed workflow management
Error characterization across heterogeneous grid sites
Identification of error patterns and failure modes
Foundation for designing effective mitigation strategies

metrics.scope: Worldwide LHC Computing Grid (WLCG), globally distributed

limitations: Analysis specific to ATLAS/LHC workloads; may not generalize to other distributed systems; retrospective analysis only (no proposed solutions in abstract).
